elaine (eng-runtime): Heads up — found a long-running memory growth issue that seems KV-cache-specific and is only reproducible on Dedicated clusters. Hosted runs stable for same load. Anyone else seen Dedicated-only kv growth?

ravi (eng-ml): Yep saw something similar last week in a customer test. Growth looks correlated with very long context traces (40k+ tokens) and repeated rollovers.

mike (eng-infra): Any chance this is a config drift between Dedicated and Hosted? We ship different oom/hugepage/mmap flags for Dedicated to match older kernels on some on-prem setups.

elaine (eng-runtime): Reproducer attached in thread: short script that sends many long chat sessions with reuse of prefixes. Behavior: memory climbs steadily (not freed), then small sudden drops when eviction triggers but fragmentation stays.

sara (customer-success): Customer on Dedicated reported similar user → high memory growth during multi-hour sessions. They ran on a private VPC with strict host kernel params.

ravi (eng-ml): Profiled heap and GPU memory with our kv-trace tool. Key observations: 1) KV metadata allocations keep increasing (alloc count grows, free count doesn't match). 2) Large contiguous allocations fail, leading to small allocations and fragmentation. 3) On Hosted we see more successful reuse of slots.

ravi (eng-ml): flamegraph snippet (trimmed):
```
KVEncode::encode_prefix  (hot)
KVStore::alloc_slot      |-- grows over time
GPUAlloc::reserve        
page_cache::shrink       (rare on Dedicated)
```

elaine (eng-runtime): I also captured per-request kernel selection logs. When sequence length jumps, we route to a larger-kernel path that allocates fresh KV buffers instead of reusing cached slots. That path is more common on Dedicated because of our routing policy that pins to local GPUs (less pool sharing).

mike (eng-infra): That routing/pinning detail is important — Dedicated has lower cross-node sharing so KV reuse across requests is lower. Combine that with slightly different munmap/madvise defaults and you get fragmentation.

elaine (eng-runtime): Hypothesis: two factors combine — (A) allocation pattern changes (big->small) cause fragmentation; (B) Dedicated kernel flags prevent madvise(MADV_DONTNEED) from returning pages promptly, so memory growth persists.

mike (eng-infra): Confirming: our Dedicated AMI uses vm.mmap_min_addr and vm.dirty_ratio tuned for on-prem perf. We also disable transparent hugepages on some clusters. That could change hugepage compaction behavior.

ravi (eng-ml): Quick experiment: toggled our KV allocator to perform explicit compact-on-free (coalesce free slots) and run with smaller bin sizes. In the Hosted test this slightly reduced tail. On Dedicated it made a big difference — steady-state memory much lower.

elaine (eng-runtime): Paste of the small alloc-coalesce change we tested:
```c
// pseudo: after free_slot(slot): try_coalesce(slot->prev, slot->next);
// reduce fallback to fresh GPUAlloc when contiguous block exists
```

sara (customer-success): The customer is okay with trying a Dedicated hotfix if it avoids rolling back to smaller contexts. They asked for a simple config toggle first.

mike (eng-infra): We should be careful: changing allocator behavior affects latency and may increase contention. Alternative: tune vm.* and madvise to proactively release pages. But in VPC/on-prem we may not have permission to change kernel params.

elaine (eng-runtime): Good point. For Private/on-prem customers we need both paths: (1) allocator-level mitigation in runtime; (2) a recommended kernel/memory tuning doc for Dedicated/Private. Hosted remains unchanged.

deploy-bot: alert: perf-regression-detect triggered for service=kv-store, window=6h, delta=+18% memory usage compared to baseline

ravi (eng-ml): I pushed a branch with the allocator coalescing and an opt-in flag: --kv-compact-on-free. Benchmarks: for our long-context load, peak GPU memory -22%, wallclock latency +2%. Numbers attached.

mike (eng-infra): Can we gate the flag behind a cluster-level config so Dedicated customers can opt-in without requiring host kernel changes? We can roll the change to a canary Dedicated pool first.

elaine (eng-runtime): Plan: 1) run the branch on a small Dedicated canary (mike) 2) collect kv-trace and flamegraphs (ravi) 3) prepare customer-facing tuning doc and opt-in flag instructions (sara + docs). I'll open a PR with tests and the reproducer.

sara (customer-success): I'll coordinate with the customer for canary on Tuesday. They prefer a non-kernel change path first.

ravi (eng-ml): A couple extra notes from profiling: - eviction thresholds on Dedicated were slightly higher (we slack memory reclaim to avoid OOMs) — lowering them reduced growth but increased eviction churn. - we also saw more short-lived small allocations from the big-kernel path; consolidating kernel selection heuristics reduced churn.

elaine (eng-runtime): Action items: ela PR w/ reproducer + opt-in flag; mike deploy canary Dedicated with flag off/on; ravi collect perf traces and compare fragmentation metrics; sara prepare customer communication + ops doc.

mike (eng-infra): I'll also dump current vm.* settings for Dedicated pools and share. Might give quick wins for those who can change kernel params.

elaine (eng-runtime): Thanks team. If anyone else sees Dedicated-only kv memory growth, drop traces here. I'll link the PR when ready. :eyes:
